9781491939369.title: Think Python: How to Think Like a Computer Scientist
9781491939369.subtitle: How to Think Like a Computer Scientist
9781491939369.publisher: O'Reilly Media (print); Green Tea Press (free edition)
9781491939369.summary: Think Python is an introduction to Python for beginners that emphasises how to think like a computer scientist: defining terms carefully, building concepts in a logical progression, and practising problem decomposition, algorithms, and debugging. The 2nd edition targets Python 3, reduces common beginner pain points, and includes a chapter on extra Python features such as list comprehensions.
whyRead: Builds programming foundations needed before machine-learning coding courses.
Free Creative Commons edition makes it easy to study without buying a print copy first.
Short chapters and exercises are designed for progressive practice, not only reading.
Widely used open textbook with matching print edition from O'Reilly.
audience: Absolute beginners to programming
Students moving into Python for data science or ML
Self-learners who want a free, structured textbook

agenda: Learn Python syntax and core data types through short exercises.
Practice writing functions, using iteration and recursion, and structuring programs.
Build fluency with strings, lists, dictionaries, files, and classes.
Develop debugging habits and a problem-solving mindset for later ML coding courses.
howToUse: Read a chapter, then run the examples and try the exercises before moving on.
Use the free HTML/PDF from Green Tea Press; use the O'Reilly print edition if you prefer paper.
Code examples and some exercise solutions are available in the companion GitHub repository described in the preface.

9780471056690.title: Pattern Classification
9780471056690.authorDisplay: Richard O. Duda, Peter E. Hart, David G. Stork
9780471056690.summary: A classic graduate-level textbook on statistical pattern recognition and classification. The 2nd edition (2000) updates the 1973 classic with material on neural networks, statistical learning theory, invariances, worked examples, comparisons between methods, and computer project topics. It remains a standard reference for Bayesian decision theory, discriminant functions, nonparametric methods, and unsupervised learning.
whyRead: Foundational theory for pattern recognition courses (e.g. D7062E AI and Pattern Recognition).
Clear Bayesian and statistical treatment of classifiers still used as the conceptual backbone of modern ML.
Covers both classical methods and multilayer neural networks in one coherent framework.
Exercises and computer projects support exam and lab preparation.
audience: Graduate and advanced undergraduate students in computer science, electrical engineering, and related fields
Researchers needing a classical reference on statistical pattern recognition
prerequisites: Comfort with mathematical notation; programming helps for computer exercises
agenda: Learn Bayesian decision theory and error-rate classification.
Estimate class-conditional densities (parametric and nonparametric).
Design linear and multilayer neural classifiers.
Apply unsupervised learning and clustering methods.
Compare algorithm-independent learning principles and evaluation ideas.
howToUse: Use as the theoretical backbone alongside applied labs and modern ML tooling.
Work chapter problems and computer exercises; a solutions manual exists for instructors.
Focus first on Chapters 2–5 for classical classification theory, then 6 and 10 for networks and clustering.

9780262043793.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
9780262043793.summary: A comprehensive machine-learning textbook for advanced undergraduates, graduates, and professionals. The substantially revised 4th edition (MIT Press, 2020) adds a full chapter on deep learning (CNNs, GANs, regularisation and structuring of deep nets), expands reinforcement learning (deep RL, policy gradients), and updates multilayer perceptrons (autoencoders, word2vec) plus dimensionality reduction (t-SNE). Appendices cover linear algebra and optimization; end-of-chapter exercises support coursework.
whyRead: Broad survey from Bayesian decision theory through kernels, graphical models, HMMs, and deep learning in one book.
Suitable companion for pattern recognition / ML electives when a single modern textbook is needed.
Balances theory and practice; widely adopted in university courses.
New deep learning and RL material in the 4th edition keeps the text current.

schmidhuber-dnn-overview.title: Deep learning in neural networks: An overview
schmidhuber-dnn-overview.subtitle: Neural Networks journal survey (2015)
schmidhuber-dnn-overview.summary: A landmark historical survey of deep learning in artificial neural networks (including recurrent nets). Published in Neural Networks Vol. 61 (Jan 2015, pp. 85–117; online 2014; DOI 10.1016/j.neunet.2014.09.003), based on arXiv:1404.7828. Distinguishes shallow vs deep learners by credit-assignment path depth and reviews supervised learning (incl. backprop history), unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning & evolutionary methods, and compressed/indirect search for large networks. Won Neural Networks’ first Best Paper Award (2017).
whyRead: Authoritative historical map of DL ideas long before the 2010s boom.
Clarifies CAP depth, vanishing gradients, LSTM, CNNs, and contest-winning lineages.
Free author page + arXiv preprint for course reading lists.
Useful complement to modern textbooks that skip early history.

prerequisites: Comfort reading survey papers with dense references

9780387008936.summary: A self-contained graduate/advanced-undergraduate introduction to the geometry of reconstructing 3-D models from collections of 2-D images. Use symmetry and step-by-step procedures to build geometric models.
